I’m not ready to start building yet—the summary captures what we explored, but a few important parts of the application remain unfinished.

I still want to work through:

- Editing the address, tags, and a personal note—not just the title and description. The note should be separate from the page’s description, support simple formatting, and display properly when I view it.
- Clicking a bookmark to open the original page, and clicking a tag to filter the collection by that tag.
- Sorting by things such as date added or title.
- Selecting several bookmarks—or all bookmarks in the current search or view—and then adding or removing tags, marking them read or unread, archiving them, or deleting them together.
- Saving a useful search and its included or excluded tags for reuse.
- Keeping a saved copy of the page in case the original disappears. For a PDF, I’d want the PDF kept instead; saving to the Internet Archive would also be useful.
- Importing my existing browser bookmarks and exporting them again without losing their titles, tags, or original saved dates.
- A few personal display choices, such as my default sorting, how many items are shown, and text size.

Those are closely connected to organising, finding, and trusting what I save, so I’d like us to explore them before implementation begins.
